extracted.intended_audience: eRA Commons users: principal investigators (PIs/PDs), signing officials (SOs), and institutional grant administrators working with NIH/DOC awards
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural guidance for using the eRA Commons Status module to view award documents, initiate/submit RPPRs and JIT packages, create and manage Revision Requests (DOC-specific), and perform award acceptance/declination. Emphasizes role-based permissions and file-upload requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additions for Review: Group categories
rubrics_metrics.description: Displays the category to which an uploaded item belongs. Categories include Updated Pages; Supplemental Material; Collaboration Letters; Modified Budget Pages; Accepted Publication; Biographical Sketches; and Other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Additions for Review section of Status Information to find additional material uploaded by the SRO. The Document column displays the file name as a link that opens the uploaded document; documents can be viewed, updated (if allowed), and saved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative Supplements: required table fields
rubrics_metrics.description: The Administrative Supplements screen displays read-only access to administrative supplements and includes columns for Identifying information (grant number link to Administrative Supplement Request PDF), Accession Number, Supplement Status, Submitted Date, and Comments for Grantee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative Supplements are requests or awards of additional funds during a current project period for increases in costs due to unforeseen circumstances. Use the Administrative Supplement History to view the read-only history.

rubrics_metrics.name: Viewing PRAM submissions order and format
rubrics_metrics.description: Progress Report Additional Materials (PRAM) opens as a PDF with a header for each PRAM submission followed by uploaded documents. If multiple submissions exist, submissions are separated with the most recent displayed first followed by earlier submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Access PRAM via Status Information -> Other Relevant Documents -> PRAM link. Agency-specific exceptions apply (e.g., DOC: Public Access PRAM not applicable).

rubrics_metrics.name: Relinquishing Statement visibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Once a relinquishing statement (part of Change of Institution) is submitted to the agency, a read-only version is available from the Commons Status Information screen. SOs can also search Status using Relinquishing Statement search type and view it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From Status search results click the award Application/Award ID, then Relinquishing Statement under Other Relevant Documents to open the Relinquishing Statement PDF.

rubrics_metrics.name: Closeout FRAM Requests visibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Closeout Final Report Additional Materials (FRAM) Requests are accessible via the Other Relevant Documents section of Status Information; users can view submitted FRAM documents by clicking Latest FRAM <date> or the linked date on the Closeout FRAM Requests screen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Closeout FRAM Requests screen to see submitted closeout materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: DOC Award Acceptance/Declination authority
rubrics_metrics.description: For Department of Commerce (DOC) awards, only a signing official (SO) can accept or decline an award. By accepting, the awardee organization agrees to all Terms and Conditions provided in the Notice of Award (NoA).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SO may optionally enter comments to agency personnel when accepting or declining. Non-DOC awards do not require formal acceptance; drawing funds is considered acceptance for non-DOC awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accept/Decline Award procedure via Status
rubrics_metrics.description: To accept or decline an award: log into eRA Commons, navigate to Status, search for award, click award's three-dot ellipsis menu and select Accept/Decline Award, then click Accept or Decline and optionally enter comments in the popup and confirm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After confirmation a green success banner appears and the Accept/Decline buttons become disabled. Follow Status Search for SOs and Awarding Office/IC filters when needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revision Requests (DOC): purpose and who can initiate
rubrics_metrics.description: DOC awardees can initiate a revision request to make changes to an existing award (e.g., assign PI/PD). Signing officials use the Status module to search for the award and choose Revision Request from the award's three-dot ellipsis menu. Revision requests are available for DOC awards only.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The feature can be used to request various changes; consult agency guidance for approvals. Initiation creates a draft request listed on Revision Request List screen.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revision Request: required fields and uploads
rubrics_metrics.description: All types of revision requests have the same fields on the Modify Request screen. The Description and Justification fields are required. The Justification document is required. You can upload up to 10 files per upload type (10 for Justification, 10 for Budget, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Request History logs when requests were saved. You may Save (to edit later) or Submit (to send to awarding agency). If business rules validations fail, error/warning messages display.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of Revision Requests and special handling
rubrics_metrics.description: DOC revision request types include: No Cost Extension - Prior Approval Required; No Cost Extension - Prior Approval Waived; Extension to Closeout; Change in Scope; Change in PI/PD; Foreign Air Carrier for Travel; Change in Key Person; Disengagement for More Than 3 Months or 25% Reduction by PI/PD; Satisfy Specific Conditions; Inclusion of Costs Requiring Prior Approval; Transfer of Funds Budgeted for Participant Support Costs; Subaward/Transfer/Contract Out Work if not described in approved application; Rebudget - Prior Approval Required; Rebudget - Prior Approval Waived; Pre-Award Costs More than 90 Days; Termination by Consent; Submit Additional Closeout Documents; ASAP Drawdown Request (ASAP Vendors Only); Other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Items with an asterisk (*) indicate that if approved, the request would result in a new Notice of Award (NoA) being generated and sent to the awardee. Use 'Other' for any request not covered in the list; such requests require program or grants office approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revision Request: saving, editing, deleting, and submission rules
rubrics_metrics.description: You may save a revision request as a draft (in-progress), continue editing it later, and delete in-progress (not-yet-submitted) revision requests. Once submitted to the awarding agency, revision requests cannot be deleted or revoked, but you can view the submitted request (Preview PDF).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To edit a saved request use Continue with Request from the three-dot ellipsis; uploaded files can be viewed or deleted via their three-dot menus. Submit requires confirmation popup; a green bar indicates successful submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: DOC RPPR: who can initiate and submit
rubrics_metrics.description: For DOC awards, only the principal investigator/program director (PD/PI) can initiate an RPPR and only a signing official (SO) can submit it. When there are multiple PIs (MPI), only the Contact PI can initiate. For DOC awards, RPPR functionality cannot be delegated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Access RPPR only via the RPPR action in the Status module for DOC awards (Manage RPPR screen does not list DOC awards).

rubrics_metrics.name: DOC RPPR: timing, sequencing, and resubmission policy
rubrics_metrics.description: RPPRs for DOC awards are due semi-annually and all DOC RPPR-eligible awards are multi-year. RPPRs should be completed/submitted in order (e.g., Semi-Annual RPPR 1 before 2). After submission, a DOC RPPR can be modified and resubmitted; a modified RPPR replaces the previously submitted RPPR until the agency accepts it. Once accepted, you cannot resubmit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The RPPR link for the current reporting period becomes available on the first day of the due period and remains available until the RPPR is submitted. If returned by DOC to awardee, the link becomes available again.

rubrics_metrics.name: DOC RPPR: J. Misc. Documents form
rubrics_metrics.description: For DOC awards, the RPPR shows an additional form named J. Misc. Documents used to upload up to 20 documents of your choice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this section to include supplemental materials relevant to the RPPR; refer to DOC grants management specialist for policy questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initiating/accessing DOC RPPR via Status module
rubrics_metrics.description: To initiate/access a DOC RPPR: navigate to Status -> List of Applications/Grants -> locate award -> select Semi-Annual RPPR <X> from Actions drop-down (Flat View). Click Initiate to begin; Commons creates RPPR in PD/PI Work in Progress status and sets initiator as current reviewer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If initiation fails due to business rules, error/warning messages appear. If an RPPR exists already, Commons displays report for editing; use three-dot ellipsis to access Edit RPPR and other actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: RPPR Menu: required metadata fields and status values
rubrics_metrics.description: The RPPR Menu screen includes fields: Award Number, PD/PI Name (Contact indicated for MPIs), Project Title, Due Date, Current Reviewer (blank before initiation), and Status (Not Started, PD/PI Work in Progress, Reviewer Work in Progress, Submitted to Agency).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Available actions (buttons/three-dot ellipsis) vary depending on RPPR status and user role; see RPPR Menu for full list.

rubrics_metrics.name: RPPR editing permission: current reviewer rule
rubrics_metrics.description: You can edit an RPPR only if you are the current reviewer. The PI who initiated the RPPR is automatically the current reviewer; when the RPPR is routed to someone else, that person becomes the current reviewer and can edit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Routing controls who can make edits; signing officials submit once appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary Statement contents available to PI/SO
rubrics_metrics.description: Summary Statements (released by the SRO) combine reviewers' written comments and the SRO's summary, including bulleted critiques from reviewers, brief summary of discussion, overall impact score, criterion scores from assigned reviewers, and more. Abbreviated review info (impact score, percentile, eligibility indicators) also appears in the Review section of Status Information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PIs view Summary Statements via Status -> List of Applications/Grants -> Application ID -> Other Relevant Documents -> Summary Statement link after release. SOs follow General search to find application and open Summary Statement similarly; impact scores are available ahead of the summary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of Award (NoA): viewing and legal significance
rubrics_metrics.description: The NoA is the legal document notifying the recipient that an award was made and funds may be requested; NoAs are sent to the Institutional Profile email and can be viewed by PIs and SOs via the Status Information screen. The Page One of the NoA serves as the first page for HSS discretionary awards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Find the NoA in Status Information -> Other Relevant Documents -> Notice(s) of Grant Award (PDF) displayed as a date link that opens the NoA in a separate window.

rubrics_metrics.name: Just in Time (JIT): role-based permissions
rubrics_metrics.description: The program director/principal investigator (PD/PI) and the signing official (SO) work together on JIT submissions: PIs may upload and save JIT information but only an SO can submit it to the funding agency. JIT capabilities cannot be delegated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If PI role, you may upload and save and view the JIT report; SO has an additional Submit button to send the package to the agency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Just in Time (JIT): submission policy and data scope
rubrics_metrics.description: The JIT screen lets you electronically submit additional application information after peer review and prior to funding. A JIT request does not guarantee funding. The requested JIT data varies based on application factors (e.g., SBIR/STTR status, human/animal subjects). Applicants should not submit JIT information until they receive a specific request from the awarding agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The JIT link becomes available for scored applications and is removed once an application is awarded. Each subsequent submission is appended to prior submissions (latest at top). SBIR/STTR Foreign Disclosure Form and DMS Plan Revision sections appear only for applicable awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: JIT: required PDF format and upload rules
rubrics_metrics.description: All JIT attachments must be submitted in PDF format with a maximum size of 6MB. Each upload area can accept only a single PDF; re-uploading replaces the previous file. All elements on the JIT form can be submitted multiple times and will be appended to the JIT report with the latest version at the top.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PDF uploads must be flattened (no fillable forms or layers). Non-flattened PDFs trigger the error: 'Error Uploading PDF. Please ensure all files are flattened....' See Flattening PDFs guidance for instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessing JIT screen (SO vs PI)
rubrics_metrics.description: To access the JIT screen: SOs use Status and perform a Just in Time or General search, then select the JIT option from the award's three-dot ellipsis menu; PIs expand a grant in Status and click the JIT button in the Available Actions column.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The JIT action is removed once an application has been awarded. You can continue submitting files while the JIT action appears; each subsequent submission appends to prior ones. Check instructions on the JIT screen for section-specific guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uploading, saving, and submitting JIT information procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: To upload files for JIT requests: access the JIT screen, use Upload buttons in each section, save an in-progress JIT by clicking Save, and SOs submit uploaded files to the agency by clicking Submit. PIs may upload and save but cannot submit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A PI can view the JIT report prepared for submission. Follow the JIT screen's top-level and section-specific instructions. Redact Personally Identifiable Information (PII) and Protected Health Information (PHI) from all uploaded documents.
